original_synthesis: Identity and value equality answer different questions. An equals implementation should honor reflexivity, symmetry, transitivity, consistency and a false comparison to null. Value-equal objects must return the same hash code, though different objects may collide. Mutating equality/hash-significant fields after inserting a key into a hash collection makes lookup behavior unreliable. Model stable business identity explicitly and choose immutable keys where practical.
misconceptions: Assuming == is the value equality test
Treating hash collisions as proof of equality
Equating business identifier semantics with Java object identity

original_mission_blueprints.original_prompt_blueprint: Distinguish reference equality from String value equality.
State the hashCode implication of equal objects, and its non-converse.
Identify a class overriding equals but not hashCode.
Assess whether two unequal objects may share a hash code.
Choose an immutable or mutable key design for an order-deduplication index.
Create a stable value key and verify lookup and equality behavior.
Diagnose an unfamiliar payment-event deduplication service that loses keys after metadata edits.

holdout: Keep final payment-event scenario separate from guided examples, exposure families and publicly practiced solutions.

Require review of explanation and business-id trade-offs.
